rows.text: homecoursesoptions trading fundamentalsintermediateoptions trading fundamentalscalls, puts, spreads and greeks — decoded for beginners.includes 5 lessons, quizzes, sources, and a completion badge. the $100,000 simulator supports spot instruments; options and futures contract mechanics are worksheet exercises.published by tradehq, created by anuga weerasinghe. publisher background and editorial approach. no independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.your progress0%earn the options fundamentals completion badge on completiona structured introduction to listed options — from call contracts and the greeks to defined-risk spread examples. work through contract payoffs on paper; tradehq's spot simulator does not execute options contracts.what you'll be able to doread an option chain and explain what a specific call or put contract obliges each side to do.estimate how a position's value changes when price, time or implied volatility moves, using delta, theta and vega rather than intuition.calculate an intact vertical spread’s theoretical expiration payoff and distinguish costs, assignment and separate stock exposure.recognise why an option can lose money even when the directional call was correct.compare hypothetical option quantities with a stated loss budget without claiming any amount is personally survivable.before you startyou should be comfortable with what a share of stock is, how a market order differs from a limit order, and what a percentage return means. no mathematics beyond arithmetic is required. if you have never placed a simulated trade, spend an hour in the practice terminal first — the options lessons assume you have seen an order ticket.how the lessons build on each otherthe track moves from object to behaviour to structure. the first lesson defines the contract itself, because almost every later misunderstanding traces back to a fuzzy definition. the greeks lesson then explains why the contract's price moves the way it does, which is what turns a static definition into something you can reason about. spread worksheets compare bounded expiration payoffs under stated assumptions, separately from assignment, costs and stock exposure. the implied-volatility lesson compares direction, time and volatility without ranking their frequency as causes of losses. the final lesson is risk management, placed last deliberately: rules only make sense once you understand what they are protecting you from.who this track is not forthis is not a track about income strategies, signal services or generating consistent weekly returns. it will not tell you which contracts to buy, and it does not cover selling naked options, which carries loss potential far beyond the premium received. if you are looking for trade recommendations rather than an explanation of how the instrument works, this material will disappoint you.lessonslesson 1what is an option? calls & puts explaineda stock option gives its buyer a contractual right; contract size, exercise style and settlement terms determine what that right involves. 8 minlesson 2the greeks — delta, gamma, theta & vegathe four greeks quantify how an option's price reacts to stock moves, volatility, and the passage of time. 10 minlesson 3defined-risk spreads — verticals & iron condorsvertical spreads and iron condors illustrate bounded expiration payoffs, with execution and assignment risks to consider. 9 minlesson 4implied volatility & trading around earningsimplied volatility is a model-implied input derived from option prices, with limits as a forecast of realised volatility. 8 minlesson 5options risk management — sizing, rolling & cutting lossesoptions losses can be amplified by position size, leverage, volatility and time decay. this lesson measures those risks using hypothetical contract examples. 9 mincompletion badgeoptions fundamentals completion: awarded after completing every lesson and submitting every quiz in the options trading fundamentals track. educational simulation only — not financial advice.all courseseducational simulation only — not financial advice. virtual money; no brokerage transactions. quotes may be delayed, cached, unavailable or fixed simulator values; generated charts are labelled separately. practice results do not predict investment outcomes.tradehq is an educational paper trading simulator. no real money is traded. nothing on this website constitutes investment, financial, legal or tax advice. past simulated performance does not predict future real-world performance.

homecoursesfutures & derivativesintermediatefutures & derivativescontracts, margin, contango and hedging — the trader's toolkit.includes 5 lessons, quizzes, sources, and a completion badge. the $100,000 simulator supports spot instruments; options and futures contract mechanics are worksheet exercises.published by tradehq, created by anuga weerasinghe. publisher background and editorial approach. no independent professional review is claimed; any recorded source-check scope appears on the page.your progress0%earn the futures fundamentals completion badge on completiona ground-up guide to exchange-listed futures — how contracts are specified, how margin actually works, why term-structure matters, and how hedgers and speculators interact on the cme.what you'll be able to doexplain what a futures contract standardises and who the natural counterparties in a market are.calculate the notional value behind a contract and the margin actually required to hold it.read a term structure and say whether a market is in contango or backwardation, and what that implies for anyone holding a rolling position.describe how a producer or consumer uses futures to hedge a real-world exposure.compare contract multipliers and notional exposure against a stated hypothetical account value; smaller contracts still carry leveraged risk.before you startsome familiarity with charts and with the idea of buying and selling an asset. the margin lesson involves multiplication and percentages, nothing more. the trading decisions and behaviour track offers optional exercises for recording assumptions. no lesson establishes a suitable real-money contract size or leverage level.how the lessons build on each otherthe sequence starts with contract specifications, then margin and leverage. term structure follows to explain differences between delivery prices and rolling exposure. hedging introduces basis risk, and micro contracts illustrate smaller multipliers. no contract size is universally suitable, and losses are not limited to the margin deposit.who this track is not forthis track does not teach day-trading systems, scalping methods or any approach that relies on high leverage to produce results. it does not cover crypto perpetual contracts, which have different funding mechanics. high notional exposure relative to account equity magnifies losses; this track does not establish a measured survival rate or a suitable real-money leverage level.lessonslesson 1what is a futures contract?a futures contract is a standardised, exchange-traded agreement to buy or sell a fixed quantity of an asset at a set price on a set future date. 8 minlesson 2margin & leverage in futuresfutures margin is collateral for contract obligations. losses and variation-margin demands can exceed an initial margin deposit. 8 minlesson 3contango & backwardation — term structure explainedcompare prices across delivery dates and study carrying costs, supply conditions and the assumptions behind rolling exposure. 9 minlesson 4hedging with futures — the original use casehedging is one use of futures. airlines may hedge fuel, producers may hedge output, and funds may hedge equity beta. 8 minlesson 5micro futures — contract size and riskcompare micro e-mini equity-index contracts with their e-mini counterparts, while checking each product’s specifications and risks. 7 mincompletion badgefutures fundamentals completion: awarded after completing every lesson in the futures & derivatives track. educational simulation only — not financial advice.all courseseducational simulation only — not financial advice. virtual money; no brokerage transactions. quotes may be delayed, cached, unavailable or fixed simulator values; generated charts are labelled separately. practice results do not predict investment outcomes.tradehq is an educational paper trading simulator. no real money is traded. nothing on this website constitutes investment, financial, legal or tax advice. past simulated performance does not predict future real-world performance.
